 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimants' challenging the judgment and award dated 18.02.2019 passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge & CJM and MACT, Kalaburagi in MVC No.407/2016 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal').
2.
We have heard the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2-insurance company and perused the materials on record.
3. The appellants/claimants are the mother and sister of deceased Mallanagouda, who died in a road traffic accident on 05.02.2016 at about 8.30 p.m.
The NC: 2023:KHC-K:7449-DB Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.8,56,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

4. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under different heads are as under:

sentences.text: In this case, the accident, death of the deceased and the liability of the Insurance company is not disputed by the respondent No.2-insurance company.
Hence, the appeal is only restricted to quantum of compensation.
The learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the MACT has quantified the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month.
However, the deceased was an agriculturist and he had annual income of Rs.15,00,000/-.
However, there is no material forthcoming in support of the said submission.

Since, the claimants have failed to produce any document to that effect, the notional monthly income of the deceased can be taken as per the Lok-Adalath chart i.e. Rs.8,750/-, considering the date of accident, i.e; 05.02.2016.
7.

Since the age of the deceased was 30 years, as per the judgment rendered in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% of the income will have to be added towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was a bachelor, half of the income is to be deducted towards personal expenses, which comes to Rs.6,125/-.
The tribunal rightly applied the multiplier 16.

On the basis of above said calculations,
compensation under the head loss of dependency is recalculated as Rs.11,76,000/-.
8. Deceased had two dependents, who is his mother and sister.
They have lost the company of their son and brother.

As held in the case of Pranay Sethi (referred supra)
and in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, Rs.44,000/- to each claimant is awarded towards loss of consortium i.e. Rs.88,000/-.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As held in the case of Pranay Sethi, Rs.16,500/- each is awarded under the head 'loss of estate' and 'funeral expenses' i.e. a total sum of Rs.33,000/-

As per above discussion, the following amount of compensation is awarded under different heads:

Thus, claimants are entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.5,45,000/- (Rs.14,01,000 - Rs.8,56,000).

9. For the above said discussion, we pass the following:
ORDER a.
The appeal is partly allowed.
b. The impugned judgment passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge & CJM and MACT Kalaburagi in MVC No.407/2016 dated 18.02.2019 is modified.

The petitioners/appellants are entitled  for a total compensation of  Rs.14,01,000/- as against  Rs.8,56,000/- awarded by the  Tribunal and they are entitled for enhancement of Rs.5,45,000/- with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till payment on the enhanced amount of compensation.
d. Respondent No.2-Insurance company is directed to deposit said amount within six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
e. The order passed by the Tribunal pertaining to apportionment, and deposit of the amount are kept intact.
